title: Tips beyond wages and splitting with the waiters
summary: She earned $17.50 then $35 in wages but hundreds in tips, and secretly dropped bills so waiters could pick them up, to avoid sharing with the musicians.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: You were telling me once about those clubs in Chicago. You got more tips than wages, right?

Oh, I didn't care about -- they didn't have to give me wages at all. Because I was only making $17.50 a week, you know, wages. And then they finally raised me to $35.00. That was a tremendous salary. Oh, my goodness, $35.00, that was a big salary. I used to get $20 bills and $50 bills, and listen, I used to go home with $400.00 and $500.00 some nights. And then we made so much, just the entertainers -- I mean the singers, that the musicians got hincty you know. And another thing
You were going between the tables?

Yeah. And they wanted us to split with them, see. So I made an agreement with the waiters, you know, that if I drop some, you pick it up and we'll split it, you know. So I would purposely drop some of that money, you know,
so the waiter would pick it up. And we'd split it in the long run.
Oh, so that afterwords you'd meet the waiter?
Oh, yeah, meet the waiter later.

Musicians didn't know it. No, what the musicians got was what I would keep in my hand, and then that was a handful, you know. I'd raise my hand up, and my hand would be full of money. But I'd accidently drop some out of one of those hands, you know, so the waiter could get it and the musicians wouldn't get it. It was a shame, but I did it just the same. I guess everything was dirty.
But anyhow, that's what I did.
